  1. Security

Security

Never commit credentials

hfSecret.token and any storage credentials belong outside version control.

helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \
  --namespace kserve \
  -f values.yaml \
  --set-string hfSecret.token="$HF_TOKEN"

Or keep secrets in a separate, ignored file:

# .gitignore
secrets.yaml

helm upgrade --install model-serving helm-charts/model-serving \
  --namespace kserve -f values.yaml -f secrets.yaml

Values supplied to Helm are stored in the release Secret. Anyone who can read Secrets in the release namespace can read a token passed through hfSecret.token. Prefer externally managed Secrets.

Externally managed Secrets 

hfSecret:
  enabled: true
  managed: false
  name: hf-secret

The chart references the Secret without creating or reading it, which works with Sealed Secrets, External Secrets Operator, and Vault injection.

External Secrets Operator example:

apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: hf-secret
  namespace: models
spec:
  secretStoreRef:
    name: vault
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
  target:
    name: hf-secret
  data:
    - secretKey: HF_TOKEN
      remoteRef:
        key: ml/huggingface
        property: token

Service accounts

The chart creates one ServiceAccount in the workload namespace:

serviceAccount:
  enabled: true
  name: hf-sa

Disable it and supply your own when your platform manages identities:

serviceAccount:
  enabled: false

models:
  - name: fraud-detector
    storageUri: s3://models/fraud/v3
    serviceAccountName: platform-managed-sa

A single ServiceAccount carries all credentials a workload needs. If a model reads from S3 and Hugging Face, attach both Secrets to that one account:

apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: combined-sa
  namespace: models
secrets:
  - name: s3-credentials
  - name: hf-secret
imagePullSecrets:
  - name: registry-credentials

Cloud identity instead of static keys

Prefer workload identity over long-lived keys.

IRSA on EKS:

apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: s3-sa
  namespace: models
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/model-reader

Workload Identity on GKE:

  annotations:
    iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: model-reader@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com

Azure Workload Identity:

  labels:
    azure.workload.identity/use: "true"
  annotations:
    azure.workload.identity/client-id: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

Private image registries 

kserve-runtime-configs:
  kserve:
    servingruntime:
      vllmserver:
        image: registry.example.com/mirror/vllm/vllm-openai
        tag: v0.11.0
        imagePullSecrets:
          - name: registry-credentials

Controllers:

kserve-resources:
  kserve:
    controller:
      imagePullSecrets:
        - name: registry-credentials

For llmInferenceServices, attach the pull secret to the ServiceAccount used in the workload namespace.

Endpoint authentication

Model endpoints do not authenticate callers. Add protection at the network or gateway layer.

Restrict which namespaces may call the models:

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: models-ingress
  namespace: models
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
  ingress:
    - from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: applications
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080

Limit outbound traffic once models are cached locally:

spec:
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
      ports:
        - protocol: UDP
          port: 53

Egress restrictions block model downloads from Hugging Face. Apply them only with pre-cached models, a PVC source, or an internal mirror.

Pod security

Upstream runtimes set restrictive container security contexts by default, including no privilege escalation and dropped capabilities. Review before relaxing:

kubectl get clusterservingruntime kserve-huggingfaceserver -o yaml | grep -A12 securityContext

The chart’s OpenVINO runtime runs as a non-root user with all capabilities dropped.

Namespaces enforcing Pod Security Standards may need the restricted profile relaxed for GPU workloads that require device access:

kubectl label namespace models pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline

Multi-tenancy

Separate teams with namespaces:

namespace: models

models:
  - name: team-a-model
    namespace: team-a
    storageUri: s3://team-a/model
    serviceAccountName: team-a-sa

  - name: team-b-model
    namespace: team-b
    storageUri: s3://team-b/model
    serviceAccountName: team-b-sa

Each namespace needs its own ServiceAccount and Secrets. Combine with network policy and resource quotas:

apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: team-a-gpu
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  hard:
    requests.nvidia.com/gpu: "4"

Supply chain

  • Pin image tags; avoid latest in production, including llmDefaults.image.
  • Pin the chart version when installing from the registry.
  • Keep Chart.lock committed so dependency digests are reproducible.
  • Mirror upstream images into a registry you control and scan them.

Review checklist 

# No plaintext tokens in tracked files
git grep -nE 'hf_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}'

# Confirm which Secrets exist in the workload namespace
kubectl get secret -n models

# Confirm no unexpected mutable tags
helm template model-serving helm-charts/model-serving -f values.yaml | grep 'image:' | sort -u
